name: Gary Kildall

summary.text: Gary Kildall (1942–1994) created the CP/M operating system and founded Digital Research Inc. When IBM sought an operating system for its Personal Computer in 1980, Digital Research's attorney declined to sign IBM's non-disclosure agreement and the company did not agree to IBM's terms; IBM instead licensed from Microsoft an operating system derived from Seattle Computer Products' 86-DOS (QDOS), which became PC-DOS. Kildall regarded 86-DOS as copied from CP/M, calling it 'plain and simple theft', and attributed CP/M-86's commercial failure to IBM pricing it at $240 against $60 for PC-DOS.

sources.title: A Career Spent In Gates' Shadow -- Computer Pioneer Dies At 52

facts.claim: When Seattle Computer Products asked about an 8086 version of CP/M, Kildall and Digital Research showed no interest in 16-bit systems at the time.
facts.quote: DR founder and software manager Gary Kildall had no interest in 16-bit systems.

facts.claim: In IBM's 1980 approach to Digital Research, DRI's attorney refused to sign IBM's non-disclosure agreement, the company declined to modify CP/M-86 and sought a higher royalty than IBM proposed.
facts.quote: DRI's attorney refused to sign the IBM non-disclosure agreement, refused to make any modifications to CP/M-86 and insisted on a higher royalty than what IBM proposed

facts.claim: Kildall described 86-DOS/QDOS as copied from CP/M, calling it 'plain and simple theft'; its author Tim Paterson has said it was his original work written to CP/M's published interface.
facts.quote: Kildall, by contrast, calls it "plain and simple theft."

sources.title: A Career Spent In Gates' Shadow -- Computer Pioneer Dies At 52

facts.claim: IBM offered CP/M-86 for the PC at $240 against $60 for PC-DOS; Kildall wrote that the pricing difference set by IBM killed CP/M-86.
facts.quote: The pricing difference set by IBM killed CP/M-86.

facts.claim: Kildall died in July 1994 at the age of 52.

sources.title: A Career Spent In Gates' Shadow -- Computer Pioneer Dies At 52

connections.claim: Microsoft licensed and then bought 86-DOS, which Kildall said was copied from his CP/M, and supplied it to IBM as PC-DOS.

sources.title: A Career Spent In Gates' Shadow -- Computer Pioneer Dies At 52

openQuestions: No Computer History Museum or IEEE page was returned; the Landley.net page is a mirror of an enthusiast history and the owner may prefer the CHM's Kildall oral history and its 2014 release of the CP/M source.
Whether 86-DOS copied CP/M code, as opposed to its published interface, has never been established in court; has any independent code comparison been published that the owner could cite?
